Subject: RFQ — Magnetic stud finder aluminum body + laser etch (Qty 100) — quote Option A (CNC) + Option B (lower-cost)

Hi {{NAME/TEAM}},

I’m requesting a quote for a small production run of a handheld magnetic stud finder body.

Attached:
1) Magnetic Stud Finder RFQ Spec (PDF)
2) Part model (STEP)
3) Magnet + assembly notes (PDF) — magnets will be sourced separately, but included for fit/assembly context
4) Reference videos (MOV/MP4)

Quantity:
- 100 units

Material / finish:
- Aluminum (open to your recommendation: 6061/7075 depending on cost and machinability)
- Laser etching for markings (no paint-fill required unless you recommend it)

Please quote two manufacturing approaches if feasible:
- Option A: CNC from billet per attached STEP file (current design)
- Option B: Lower-cost approach using plate/sheet stock + laser/waterjet profile + minimal secondary ops (if you think it can meet functional requirements). If Option B isn’t feasible, no problem—please note why.

Critical dimensions:
- Overall length/width
- The top notch that holds the pen/marker
(Other dimensions are less critical as long as the part is functional and comfortable in-hand.)

What I need in the quote:
- Unit price @ 100 units
- One-time setup/NRE (if any)
- Lead time to first articles + lead time for the batch
- Any DFM feedback (especially to make Option B possible)
- Recommended tolerances for the critical dimensions above
- Laser etch cost assumptions (setup + per-unit)

Questions:
- What aluminum thickness/stock would you recommend for durability while keeping cost down?
- If we want to keep the body aluminum but avoid heavy CNC time, what design changes would you suggest?
- If you can also do finishing (anodize) economically, please include an alternate quote line for anodize + laser.

If you’re the wrong contact, could you point me to whoever handles CNC/laser + small production runs?

Thanks,
Grayson
